## 邮件 1 → Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli (rafagb@mit.edu)

**Subject:** Exploring AI-driven catalyst design collaboration — Beihang University / Heguang Zhicheng

Dear Professor Gómez-Bombarelli,

I hope this message finds you well. I am Prof. Yuzhou Liu (刘宇宙) at Beihang University's School of Chemistry, and also the founder of Heguang Zhicheng, a startup focused on AI-powered materials science.

I have been following your work at the Learning Matter Lab with great admiration — particularly the recent DiffSyn paper in *Nature Computational Science* (2026), which elegantly bridges generative AI with materials synthesis planning. Your vision of combining physics-based simulations with machine learning to accelerate materials discovery resonates deeply with our research philosophy.

At Beihang, our group has been developing AI-driven approaches for catalyst design, particularly in the areas of heterogeneous catalysis and electrocatalysis. We have built computational-experimental pipelines that integrate DFT calculations, machine learning descriptors, and high-throughput screening — work that I believe could complement your group's generative design capabilities.

I would be very interested in exploring potential collaboration opportunities between our groups. Specifically, I see exciting synergies in:
- Applying generative models (like DiffSyn) to catalyst precursor design
- Combining your simulation-based screening with our experimental catalysis validation
- Joint grant proposals bridging AI and sustainable catalysis

If you are open to it, I would love to arrange a brief virtual meeting to discuss potential synergies. I would also be honored to invite you to visit Beihang University in Beijing as a visiting scholar.

Thank you for your time, and congratulations again on your well-deserved tenure.

Warm regards,

Prof. Yuzhou Liu (刘宇宙)
